notes: ABox contraction on a functional, symmetric relation (antiparticle_of), paired with physics-replace-0002: removes "The antiparticle of the proton is the antiproton", a stored fact. Cardinality question: is the positron the proton's antiparticle (no before, since a particle has one antiparticle). Caveat: "the positron is the electron's antiparticle" is stored everywhere, so "no" can survive a perfect removal. The one related question asks which particle, together with a positron, makes up an antihydrogen atom (a stored fact about a different individual, the antihydrogen atom, reached through the proton's antiparticle and the electron's): antiproton before, "I don't know" after, since an ideal contraction gives up the supporting knowledge too; it is the revision's related question. The two 2-hop derived questions are the century of discovery of the proton's antiparticle (composition) and the antiparticle of the hydrogen nucleus (binding); the latter has a route through antihydrogen being described as an antiproton plus a positron. Name caveat: "antiproton" means the proton's antiparticle, so a model can rebuild the removed fact from the word. antiparticle_of has no inverse axiom, so there is no inverse related question. The revision's mass question is not reused, since an antiparticle has its particle's mass.
